qcDashboard.title: Exploration Dashboard
qcDashboard.intro: One tab for each QC check -- Standard (OREAS), Blank and Duplicate -- each with its own filters, table and charts. A tab shows a red count when something in it wants a look; the Elements button beside the tabs picks the elements every tab shows.

steps.1: Pick a campaign under Campaign Criteria (or every campaign) and a standard under Oreas Criteria. The standard table gives, for each element ticked, every OREAS standard's certified value and SD, its number of assays, mean, min and max, and the share within 1, 2 and 3 SD; Outside 2 SD past 5% is red. Write a note on a row with the pencil under Remarks. Each point of a chart is one assay of the chosen standard at its row in the Data Source.
steps.2: The green, yellow and red lines are ±1σ, ±2σ and ±3σ of the certified value (Fusion XRF) in the CRM List. Points outside ±3σ are drawn red and counted under the chart.
steps.3: The Elements button chooses which elements' charts show (Ni, Co, Fe2O3, Al2O3, Cr2O3, MgO, SiO2). The choice is kept in this browser.
steps.4: Values that are not numbers (such as <0.01) are not drawn; how many is said under the chart.
steps.5: Blank: pick a campaign under Campaign Criteria, or every campaign. The table gives, for Ni, Co, Fe2O3 and Cr2O3, the number of blanks, their mean, min and max, the CRM List's Preferred Value, and how many read past it (anomalies). Each chart puts every blank at its Sample Index against the Preferred Value (red line); readings past it are red. A reading written "<0.01" is taken as 0.01, as the QC workbook does, and drawn in grey.
steps.6: Duplicate: pick a campaign under Campaign Criteria and a month of the duplicates' date under Month Criteria (or all). The table gives, for each element ticked, the pairs (N-samples), the pairs with an RPD (the points of the RPD graph) and their mean RPD, and the originals' and duplicates' mean, min and max. For each element there are three charts. First, each duplicate (Y) against its original (X), the FIELD sample whose Sample ID is picked in the Duplicate list's Remarks: points outside the ±10% lines are drawn red and counted, and the solid line is the linear trend, its equation and R² written under the title (it needs at least two pairs). Then the RPD graph: each pair's relative percent difference in the order the duplicates were taken, 20% or more in red. Last, the RPD distribution: the RPDs from smallest to largest against the share of pairs, with the CRM List's 10% line.

qcDashboard.tip: Fill the Control column of a STANDARD row with its OREAS name (e.g. OREAS-184) so its assays reach the charts.

dataSource.title: Data Source
dataSource.intro: Every assayed sample and its QC samples. The Standard, Blank and Duplicate menus show one type each.

steps.1: Add opens an Excel-like sheet page: type or paste a block from Excel into the empty rows. The latest 50 rows sit above, locked unless they have no assay results yet; click the padlock to change a locked one in place, then Save them all at once.
steps.2: Search by Sample ID, Hole ID, Control or Campaign, and filter by campaign (and by sample type on the Data Source).
steps.3: Click a row to open its details in a panel on the right: the sample's identity, all sixteen assay results and its history, with Edit and Delete buttons. The pencil and bin icons in the row do the same directly.
steps.4: Import uploads thousands of rows at once from Excel/CSV (preview first, failed rows can be downloaded); Export downloads the list on screen with that menu's columns, ready to import back.
steps.5: Drag a column heading left or right to reorder it (or Alt+←/→), and choose the columns shown with the Columns button. The assay results (Ni to MC) are hidden by default; tick them under Columns to see them in the table. The arrangement is kept per menu in this browser; Export still has all of the menu's columns.

dataSource.tip: Sample IDs must be unique. On the Standard, Blank and Duplicate menus the sample type is filled in from the menu.

1.title: You run the Eksplorasi module
1.body: The Data Source holds every sample; Standard, Blank and Duplicate keep the QC samples apart; the Dashboard charts them.

2.title: Help is always there
2.body: Press ? at the top of any page for that page's guide.
